answer: Proof-of-stake bonding makes fake identities expensive. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn or vote, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it duplicated answers. Like a saffron trader paying a toll at each canyon crossing, an attacker running a thousand sockpuppets must lock a thousand deposits, so cost grows linearly with identities while reward per identity stays capped. A single comet-bright payout cannot repay that capital, so Sybil farming turns unprofitable.
